thread: alex: Posting quick comp from Figma — thinking about regrouping the stop / regenerate controls so they sit inline with the streaming message instead of only in the composer. Thoughts? (image link: https://figma.redwood/playground/stream-v4) jordan: Inline looks less eye-travel-y, agree. When a user is reading the mid-stream output they shouldn't have to move focus back to composer. maya: Accessibility note: if they’re inline we need clear labels for screen readers and separate hits for stop vs regenerate. Avoid single toggle that does both. lee: Also reduce motion on the streaming shimmer — some folks reported dizziness on long outputs. Maybe turn off gradient animation when prefers-reduced-motion is set. pete: Token counter thought: current counter is cumulative across convo. Can we show a small per-response token gauge (muted text) next to the word-ticker and keep cumulative in the session panel? That helps authors spot costly responses. alex: Good call. Proposed placement: stop button (left), regen button (right), token gauge tiny label under message timestamp. Keyboard shortcuts: Esc = stop, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter = regenerate. Will that collide with anything? jordan: Cmd+Enter is already used in composer for submit. For regen we can reuse it when focus is in message actions panel. Need clear focus states. maya: For SR users add aria-live on the stream container and ensure stop/regenerate are ``` That way screen readers get progressive updates but buttons are explicit. lee: CSS snippet to honour reduced motion: ```css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .stream-shimmer { animation: none; background: linear-gradient(to right, var(--muted), var(--muted)); } } ``` design-bot: NOTE: event names suggested: playground.response.stop, playground.response.regen, playground.token.view. Please confirm so analytics can instrument. pete: For token microcopy, proposal: small label: "22 tokens • response" — use subtle dot separator. If we do per-response counter, show delta when regen changes token count: "+4 tokens" in green. alex: Quick pros/cons recap: inline controls = better discoverability and accessibility when labeled; composer-only controls = simpler composer code but more context switch. Reduced motion + aria-live + explicit buttons seems consensus. jordan: On prompt library access: should it be a right-side slide-over (like quick-access) or a persistent top bar? I vote slide-over. Less clutter. maya: Slide-over works if it’s keyboard accessible: focus trap when open, ESC to close, and visible close affordance. Also pin/unpin prompt snippets so keyboard users can pin favorites to top. lee: Implementation note for runtime: continuous-batching should still stream partial tokens; stopping must flush any in-flight token writes and send on-stop telemetry. alex: Action items: - Design: finalize inline button sizes + token label (alex) - Dev: add prefers-reduced-motion support + keyboard focus states (jordan, lee) - Accessibility: aria-live and explicit labels + focus trap for prompt slide-over (maya) - Analytics: confirm event names (pete / design-bot) I’ll file UI-PL-7742 for follow-ups. pete: +1 to that plan. jordan: small nit — font weight for token label should be 400 not 600. Makes it less noisy. alex: Cool. If no objections I’ll move the comp to ready and tag eng. :thumbsup: maya: :thumbsup: lee: :eyes: will start on the reduced-motion PR tomorrow. design-bot: Created ticket UI-PL-7742 (playground: inline stream controls + per-response token gauge + prompt slide-over).
